newsitem.title: PERU: Shell, Intergen sign Peru power plant memorandum.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Intergen sign Peru power plant memorandum.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group said Thursday it signed with U.S. firm International Generating Co (Intergen) a memorandum of understanding for the development of a power plant fueled by Peru's Camisea gas.
In April, Shell chose Intergen to join it in developing a plant with a capacity of between 300 megawatt (MW) and 600 MW.
Shell is the operating partner of a joint venture with Mobil developing the huge Camisea natural gas fields.
Intergen and the oil consortium have formed a new company, EnerPeru S.R.L., "to build, own, and operate the new power facility", Shell said in a statement.
EnerPeru estimates the plant's construction will begin in 1998 ready for operations to start in 2000 and become "a competitive source of electricity for southern Peru", Shell added.
Shell is halfway through a license to explore the Camisea reserves. The oil giant hopes to begin early production in 1999 and bring gas to Lima by pipeline in 2001.
